messages.subject: set.seed generates different outputs
parts:
Dear all,

Apologies if this has been covered elsewhere - I did search.

I have some code that generates clusters using a stochastic process. Thus, I use set.seed(10) to get a consistent output. This works fine on my own computer, and works fine on the shinyapps.io side. The issue is that the results are not consistent across the two. I get different results if I run the same code from both sources, even in the same browser window.

My understanding is that I should get the same output in both cases. Any insights into why this might be occurring? Or even better - how to fix it?

Thanks in advance,

Damien

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] set.seed generates different outputs
parts:
Hi Winston,

Thank you for getting back to me. I failed when trying to make a minimal reproducible example. Not because I couldn't make one, but because I couldn't reproduce the behaviour using simple R functions.

So this led me to dig a bit deeper. The function I am having troubles with is Rtsne, which generates different outputs on my side and on the shinyapps.io side. The package relies on Rcpp. First thing I did was to update the Rcpp to the latest version - lo and behold this changed my output (given the same seed)! However, interestingly it didn't change the output on the shinyapps.io side. I checked and the R version, and Rtsne and Rcpp package versions, are the same on both sides (my computer and shinyapps.io).

My current thinking is that I'm running OSX here, and presumably the shinyapps.io R session(s) are being run on a different OS. This makes me think that the differences could lie deeper in the C++ side of things?

Any further advice would be welcome.

Damien
